reproduction:
python3 -c "import asyncio; from falcon.asgi import Request; from falcon import testing; async def m():
    scope = testing.create_scope(); scope['client'] = None
    print(Request(scope, None).remote_addr)
asyncio.run(m())"
observed_failure_at_parent: TypeError: cannot unpack non-iterable NoneType object (raised from falcon/asgi/request.py when accessing remote_addr/access_route because scope['client'] is None instead of missing); regression test test_client_none_in_scope: 1 failed
verified: both directions observed in a bench-base:python-3.12 container at /tmp/falcon. PARENT bc01a2b: git reset --hard + git clean -fd, grep proves 'except KeyError:' (no TypeError) present at line ~220; direct repro raises TypeError and pytest test_client_none_in_scope FAILS. FIX a54317c7: grep proves 'except (KeyError, TypeError):' present; direct repro prints remote_addr: 127.0.0.1 and the same pytest test PASSES.
install_recipe: cd <repo> && pip install pytest && pip install -e .
issue_paraphrase: When an ASGI server is bound such that the connection scope carries no peer address (for example a Unix domain socket or some proxy setups), reading the request's remote address attribute raises a TypeError ("cannot unpack non-iterable NoneType object") instead of falling back to the 127.0.0.1 default used when the address field is absent. Any application or middleware that logs or inspects the client address then crashes on such requests.
fix_summary: Catch TypeError alongside KeyError when unpacking scope['client'] in the cached access-route property, defaulting to '127.0.0.1'.
notes: pure Python, no network, no extra deps; single test, suite for the test file is ~instant. Regression test exists at tests/asgi/test_request_asgi.py::test_client_none_in_scope and imports fine with base deps only.

issue_paraphrase: Customizing which media handlers (e.g. JSON, msgpack) a multipart parser uses leaks into every other multipart parser created in the same process: removing or replacing a handler on one upload parser silently removes it for all others, so unrelated requests suddenly fail to parse or render upload parts with the wrong serializer. The configuration mutation should be isolated per parser instance.
fix_summary: Initialize MultipartParseOptions.media_handlers from a per-instance copy of the default handlers (added a Handlers.copy() method and used it in the constructor).
notes: pure Python, no network; tests/test_media_multipart.py needs optional handler libs (ujson/msgpack/cbor2) only in try/except paths; with pip install pytest only (plus falcon itself) the file collects and runs. Direct repro is a tiny standalone script; 107 other tests in the file are deselected by -k.

observed_failure_at_parent: RAW_URI '/' (hardcoded) while PATH_INFO == '/cache/http://falconframework.org/status'; regression test test_create_environ_preserve_raw_uri FAILS with AssertionError at tests/test_testing.py:171
verified: both directions observed in a bench-base:python-3.12 container at /tmp/falcon. PARENT 7191be4: git reset --hard + git clean -fd, grep proves 'RAW_URI': '/' literally hardcoded in create_environ; direct repro prints RAW_URI = / and the regression test FAILS. FIX 69cdcd6e: grep proves 'RAW_URI': raw_path where raw_path = path captured before decoding; repro prints the full raw percent-encoded path; test PASSES.
install_recipe: cd <repo> && pip install pytest && pip install -e .
issue_paraphrase: The test harness's request-environment builder always reports the raw request URI as a single slash, no matter which path was requested. This diverges from real WSGI servers (wsgiref, gunicorn, uWSGI), which expose the raw percent-encoded path before decoding. Applications that route or sign URLs using the raw path see correct behavior under a real server but wrong behavior under the framework's test client, so tests fail for features involving percent-encoded characters such as encoded slashes inside path segments.
fix_summary: In falcon/testing/helpers.py create_environ, capture the original path before percent-decoding and use it for the RAW_URI environ variable instead of the literal '/'.
notes: pure Python, no network. tests/test_testing.py imports only pytest + falcon.testing. Direct repro standalone. 42 other tests in the file deselected by -k.

observed_failure_at_parent: root_path '/cafÃ©' (latin-1 mojibake: WSGI SCRIPT_NAME handed through raw, so the accented char appears as two iso-8859-1 glyphs instead of one UTF-8 char); regression test test_root_path_non_ascii_wsgi FAILS

FIX ce0a35b8: grep proves the non-ASCII branch 'if not root_path.isascii(): root_path = root_path.encode("iso-8859-1").decode("utf-8", "replace")'; repro prints '/café'; test PASSES.
install_recipe: cd <repo> && pip install pytest && pip install -e .
issue_paraphrase: When a WSGI application is mounted under a URL prefix that contains non-ASCII characters (for example accented letters), the value reported for the app's root/mount path is mojibake: the raw Latin-1-encoded string is returned without the UTF-8 re-decoding that is applied to the request path itself, so path values end in an ISO-8859-1 double-shot like 'Ã©' instead of 'é'. Routing and URL reconstruction that use the mount prefix then break for such deployments.
fix_summary: Decode a non-ASCII WSGI SCRIPT_NAME from ISO-8859-1 to UTF-8 (with replace) before returning it as Request.root_path, mirroring the PATH_INFO handling per PEP 3333.
notes: pure Python, no network. Golden test lives in tests/test_request_attrs.py (a parametrized module; -k selects the single new test). Request must be constructed with a WSGI environ dict; falcon.Request(env) works. 282 other tests in the file deselected by -k.

reproduction: PYTHONPATH=/tmp/falcon python3 -c "from falcon.cyutil.uri import decode; print(repr(decode('+00', unquote_plus=False)))"  (requires the Cython-compiled extension built from the checkout; pure-Python install does NOT reproduce — see notes)
observed_failure_at_parent: '\x00' instead of '+00' — a literal plus followed by two hex digits is misread as a percent-encoded byte when unquote_plus=False, so e.g. decode('2026-06-29T23:11:38.964935+00:00.jpg', unquote_plus=False) == '2026-06-29T23:11:38.964935\x00:00.jpg' (NUL byte injected, and a str could be truncated at it); pytest tests/test_utils.py -k uri_decode_unquote_plus: 2 failed (bytearray, join_list variants), 1 passed (str variant)
verified: both directions observed in a bench-base:python-3.12 container at /tmp/falcon, with gcc + Cython installed and 'python3 setup.py build_ext --inplace' after each reset. PARENT 6566f4a: git reset --hard + git clean -fd, grep proves the buggy condition 'if data[pos] == b'+' and unquote_plus:' in falcon/cyutil/uri.pyx; direct repro prints '\x00' and the two parametrized variants FAIL. FIX 7f55a5eb: git reset --hard + git clean -fd, grep proves the '+' is now handled unconditionally with the unquote_plus check nested inside; direct repro prints '+00' (and ' 00' with unquote_plus=True, timestamp unchanged); all three parametrized variants PASS.
install_recipe: apt-get update && apt-get install -y gcc && pip install Cython && pip install -e . --no-build-isolation (then, if needed: python3 setup.py build_ext --inplace)  — bench-base:python-3.12 has NO gcc by default, so install_recipe MUST include the apt line or reproduce via a released wheel instead
issue_paraphrase: URL decoding with plus-to-space conversion disabled mishandles a literal plus sign when it is immediately followed by two hexadecimal digits: it is treated as a percent-encoding escape and replaced by the decoded byte. A timestamp with a UTC offset such as '+00:00' in a path therefore injects a NUL byte into the decoded value. Only the compiled (accelerated) code path is affected; the pure-Python behavior is correct.
fix_summary: In the Cython implementation of uri.decode, handle b'+' explicitly: only translate it to a space when unquote_plus is enabled, otherwise copy it through and never let it fall into the percent-decoding branch.
notes: REPRODUCIBILITY DEPENDS ON THE COMPILED EXTENSION. (a) pip install falcon from PyPI installs a prebuilt wheel that includes the affected compiled module, so a task pinned to a released buggy falcon would reproduce out of the box; (b) installing from source is pure-Python on bench-base:python-3.12 unless gcc + Cython are installed first — the direct repro then fails with ImportError pretending the bug is gone. If authoring from source, the image must install gcc (and Cython) first. The golden test runs the str variant through the pure-Python path (passes even at parent); only bytearray/join_list variants of test_uri_decode_unquote_plus fail at parent. Use the direct-repro assertion (decode('+00', unquote_plus=False) == '+00') as the oracle string, not the pytest selection alone.
